title: POV: chameleon, misunderstood

scenes.headline: POV: you're a chameleon and everyone thinks you change colour to hide
You actually do it to show off to rivals and mates
It's tiny crystals in your skin
scenes.body: Panther chameleons tune a lattice of guanine nanocrystals in skin cells, changing which colours of light bounce back.

caption:
Camouflage is the background. The colour show is the message.

Relaxed male panther chameleons look mostly green; when excited, the crystal spacing widens and they shift toward yellow and orange.

Source: Teyssier et al. 2015, Nature Communications.  Photos/video: Wikimedia Commons (credits on screen).
notes: POV myth-buster: first-person complaint about a common misconception, resolved with the 2015 photonic-crystal finding; panther chameleon photo matches the studied species.
